newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on exports, crush data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on exports, crush data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on Friday, supported by strong USDA weekly export sales data and U.S. Census crush figures, traders said.
USDA on Friday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans during the week ended January 16 totaled 447,000 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
But some traders downplayed the significance of the export data, saying it represented historical information that had already been factored into the market.
"We all got very excited here about export sales but it's history," a trader said. "It's already covered in the market."
The U.S. Census Bureau monthly oilseed crush report also lent support and confirmed ideas soybean consumption remained strong despite rising prices, traders said.
The report showed there were 138 million bushels of soybeans crushed in December, up from 133 million bushels in November and above expectations for 137 million, traders said.
The Census report showed U.S. soybean stocks fell to 105.4 million bushels from 117.4 million bushels in November and 119.7 million last year.
Soybeans closed 6-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 6-1/4 at $7.47-1/2.

On the day, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought at least eight million bushels and Refco Inc bought two million March, traders said. Iowa Grain, Prudential Securities and Lee B. Stern each bought one million March, sources said.
ADM sold two million March while Cargill Inc bought one million March and sold 1.5 million March, traders said.
In options, Lind-Waldock bought 1,000 $7.50 May calls in late dealings. Cargill Investor Services bought 800 $7.25 March puts, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, according to CBOT data. That compared with Thursday's actual volume of 43,876 contracts.
